text:
AI-generated animation · made with AniMus · 8:01 · English

Turn Around

Beyond the Cave

He knows every shadow on the wall. Then someone asks him to turn around.
Plato’s cave becomes a musical story about being wrong, finding your feet, and going back for your friends.

[[Open in AniMus|Turn Around · AniMus]][[Script|Turn Around · Script]][[Music|Turn Around · Music]][[Scenes|Turn Around · Scenes]][[About and credits|Turn Around · About]]
<$plato-player film="Turn Around · Complete performance (film)"/>

An AI-generated AniMus demonstration and an editable practice project. Open it in AniMus to combine your own audio recordings, music and animation. The characters, shots, script, scores and audio clips are available to work with.

I · SCENES 01–05

Never wrong

A lifelong view of one wall. Familiar voices. Correct predictions. A chain opens, and the expert suddenly knows nothing.

II · SCENES 06–10

One more step

A climb nobody asked for. Too much light. A face in the water. Bigger questions — and the friends still waiting below.

III · SCENES 11–14

Room for two

Home is harder than he expected. They see a failure. He sees people he loves. What does knowing more ask of him?

14 editable scenes · four songs · painted Greek settings · articulated cutout and drawn animation
An original adaptation of Plato’s Republic, Book VII. A demonstration of AniMus, made with AI-generated media.

title: Turn Around · Scenes
text:
[[Watch the performance|Turn Around]][[Open in AniMus|Turn Around · AniMus]][[Script|Turn Around · Script]][[Music|Turn Around · Music]]

The same Greek characters and painted settings appear in a faster English rewrite. Choose a chapter in the player, or open AniMus to change the scenes and their timing.

01 · 0:00–0:26

The Whole World

Open directly on the chained prisoners, then pull back to reveal the vast limestone cave. Cut between ankle irons, a restrained neck and the older prisoner's dry expression. Keep the fire out of their sight.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 01 · The Whole World]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 01 · The Whole World]]

02 · 0:26–0:58

Voices on the Wall

A horse, jar and bird pass as shadows. Follow the bird, then reveal the actual objects carried behind a low wall. One clean wide shot establishes fire, carriers, prisoners and shadow wall. Drawn fire and echo contours animate over cutout figures.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 02 · Voices on the Wall]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 02 · Voices on the Wall]]

03 · 0:58–1:52

Never Wrong

The parade returns in a tight rhythmic pattern. The prisoner anticipates the jar with smug precision; the elder replies with a sidelong look. During the first chorus, the shadows become an insistent red-figure pottery frieze.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 03 · Never Wrong]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 03 · Never Wrong]]

04 · 1:52–2:18

Up You Get

Cut close to the lock and the guide's hand. Release, wobble, a caught fall: let the physical comedy interrupt the solemn moment. The prisoner's neck then turns painfully. The guide remains a plainly dressed classical Greek woman.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 04 · Up You Get]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 04 · Up You Get]]

05 · 2:18–2:43

The Real Thing

Turn with the prisoner towards the fire. Soft glare, then the small real jar held against its huge shadow. The guide moves it nearer the flame while the prisoner protests. Keep the demonstration readable in one composed shot.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 05 · The Real Thing]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 05 · The Real Thing]]

06 · 2:43–3:34

One More Step

Accelerate the climb through diagonals: gripping fingers, slipping sandals, rising dust and a wide view of the steep passage. The guide steadies and pulls the reluctant prisoner. The chorus gives the movement a firm forward pulse.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 06 · One More Step]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 06 · One More Step]]

07 · 3:34–4:03

Too Much Light

Daylight briefly washes out the landscape, without flashing. Cut down to the hand's shadow, then a pool. Let the guide's joke land before the prisoner touches his reflection. Hand-drawn ripples break the face into moving lines.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 07 · Too Much Light]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 07 · Too Much Light]]

08 · 4:03–4:29

The Other Side

Match a reflection to the actual olive tree. The prisoner circles its trunk and discovers its hidden side. A compact transition carries the scene into moonlight and stars. His sense of space expands; the camera finally has room to breathe.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 08 · The Other Side]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 08 · The Other Side]]

09 · 4:29–5:19

What Makes Seeing Possible

Show the sun through what it changes: leaves, water, warm skin and travelling shadows. Use a restrained stylised sun rather than sustained staring at it. The third chorus opens the frame and transforms the earlier shadow shapes into visible things.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 09 · What Makes Seeing Possible]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 09 · What Makes Seeing Possible]]

10 · 5:19–5:41

The Ones Below

Give the prisoner a quiet beat beneath the olive tree. A strip of shadow recalls the cave. The guide offers him the open landscape; he turns towards the entrance instead. End on the decisive first step back.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 10 · The Ones Below]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 10 · The Ones Below]]

11 · 5:41–6:04

Home Again

Repeat the cave's opening compositions with the returned prisoner stumbling through them. His view is dark and uncertain. Cut sharply from the elder's challenge to the old procession, which continues without him.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 11 · Home Again]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 11 · Home Again]]

12 · 6:04–6:31

Hands Off My Chain

Tight faces, a hand approaching a chain, a sudden recoil. The elder's defensive anger fills the frame. Hold before any blow: the threat remains hypothetical. Let the shadows loom while the actual people stay frightened and human.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 12 · Hands Off My Chain]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 12 · Hands Off My Chain]]

13 · 6:31–7:00

Same Eyes, Bigger Questions

Simplify the frame into cutout bodies and drawn intermediate poses. Head, shoulders and feet turn together. Briefly compare the two kinds of blindness: entering brightness and re-entering darkness. Keep the explanation moving through visible action.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 13 · Same Eyes, Bigger Questions]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 13 · Same Eyes, Bigger Questions]]

14 · 7:00–8:01

Room for Two

Connect the cave and the daylight in one final spatial image. The prisoner sits beside the elder at equal height. A hand approaches the chain, but no miraculous mass release occurs. Finish with the chorus, a narrow moving line of light and the title.

[[Scene data|Turn Around · 14 · Room for Two]] · [[Score|Turn Around · Score · 14 · Room for Two]]

title: Turn Around · Music
text:
[[Watch the performance|Turn Around]][[Open in AniMus|Turn Around · AniMus]][[Script|Turn Around · Script]][[Music|Turn Around · Music]]
The four songs return to the words ''Turn around''. At first the chorus resists the idea. Later it urges the prisoner forward, welcomes a larger world, and makes room for someone else. !! Songs * [[Never Wrong|Turn Around · Vocal score · 03]] * [[One More Step|Turn Around · Vocal score · 06]] * [[What Makes Seeing Possible|Turn Around · Vocal score · 09]] * [[Room for Two|Turn Around · Vocal score · 14]] !! Instrumental scores * [[01 · The Whole World|Turn Around · Score · 01 · The Whole World]] * [[02 · Voices on the Wall|Turn Around · Score · 02 · Voices on the Wall]] * [[03 · Never Wrong|Turn Around · Score · 03 · Never Wrong]] * [[04 · Up You Get|Turn Around · Score · 04 · Up You Get]] * [[05 · The Real Thing|Turn Around · Score · 05 · The Real Thing]] * [[06 · One More Step|Turn Around · Score · 06 · One More Step]] * [[07 · Too Much Light|Turn Around · Score · 07 · Too Much Light]] * [[08 · The Other Side|Turn Around · Score · 08 · The Other Side]] * [[09 · What Makes Seeing Possible|Turn Around · Score · 09 · What Makes Seeing Possible]] * [[10 · The Ones Below|Turn Around · Score · 10 · The Ones Below]] * [[11 · Home Again|Turn Around · Score · 11 · Home Again]] * [[12 · Hands Off My Chain|Turn Around · Score · 12 · Hands Off My Chain]] * [[13 · Same Eyes, Bigger Questions|Turn Around · Score · 13 · Same Eyes, Bigger Questions]] * [[14 · Room for Two|Turn Around · Score · 14 · Room for Two]] The vocal performances are generated by a trained singing model. The vocal scores are editable transcriptions of those takes. Instrumental parts use original digital sounds inspired by lyra, kithara, aulos and frame drum. The composition is a modern interpretation of ancient Greek musical colours. Audio takes are stored in the wiki. AniMus’ native audio timeline controls their start, trim, duration, volume and mute state. The audience player reads that same film and audio timeline. Separate sound controls adjust speech, singing and music.

title: Turn Around · About
text:
[[Watch the performance|Turn Around]][[Open in AniMus|Turn Around · AniMus]][[Script|Turn Around · Script]][[Music|Turn Around · Music]]
!! An AI-generated AniMus demonstration ''Turn Around — Beyond the Cave'' is an AI-generated animation made with AniMus. Its purpose is to demonstrate what AniMus can do and to give users an editable project for combining audio recordings, music, dialogue and animation. The writing, illustrations, generated voices, singing, music and animation were created with AI assistance. The project can be opened and changed in AniMus. It is also a complete performance that can be watched without entering the editor. !! The adaptation This is an original English rewrite after Plato’s ''Republic'', Book VII, 514a–521b. It follows the prisoners, fire, carrying wall, shadows and echoes; the painful release; the forced ascent; the gradual adjustment to light; the return; the ridicule and threat; and the responsibility to return to the community. The guide as a woman, the individual dialogue, humour, songs and open ending are new dramatic choices. The sun stands for the Good. The threatened killing is described as Plato’s question, not shown as a completed event. !! What you can edit Characters remain articulated CutOut parts. Backdrops are replaceable image parts. Fire, dust, water and stars use editable drawing frames. Camera keys and scene timings remain in the native scenes. Dialogue and lyrics are text cues in the native Script workshop. Each spoken recording is its own linked audio clip. Scores remain ABC tiddlers. The audience player follows the native film. Saved changes to scene order, source timing, camera, parts, captions and audio clips appear there. The audio engine uses embedded recordings and continues with a silent visual clock if audio cannot run. Speech mouth timing combines recorded word markers, English pronunciation groups and measured energy. Singing uses timing extracted from the vocal performance. These are animation cues rather than a claim of perfect phoneme recognition. When an original line or take is replaced, obsolete mouth timing falls back to the editable script timing. !! Credits and sources * [[Plato · Republic, Book VII · Benjamin Jowett translation|https://classics.mit.edu/Plato/republic.8.vii.html]] — narrative source; English dialogue and lyrics here are newly written. * [[The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Music in Ancient Greece|https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/music-in-ancient-greece]] — historical instrument context. * [[Oxford TORCH · Recreating the Music of an Ancient Greek Chorus|https://torch.web.ox.ac.uk/article/recreating-the-music-of-an-ancient-greek-chorus-euripides-orestes]] — research into ancient choral music. * [[ACE-Step|https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5]] — trained music generation model used for original vocal performances. Model and rendering details are recorded in [[Singing provenance|Turn Around · Singing provenance]]. * English neural speech voices: Ryan, Thomas, Sonia and Christopher. The generated recordings are embedded; playback does not contact a speech service. * [[CMU Pronouncing Dictionary|https://github.com/cmusphinx/cmudict]] — English pronunciation data used to guide approximate mouth shapes. * [[AniMus and HUWiki Forge|https://github.com/maans/huwiki-forge]] — AniMus, CutOut and HUWiki ABC, running in TiddlyWiki 5.4.1. Included components retain their own notices and licences. The music is historically inspired, with newly generated digital timbres. It is not presented as a reconstruction of a surviving ancient performance.
